summary: Heinrich Wenzel (1855–1893) was an Indologist and Tibetologist. He studied at Jena, Tübingen (PhD c. 1878–1879), and Leipzig (Habilitation c. 1886), as well as under H. A. Jäschke, L. Feer, G. von der Gabelentz, and F. Max Müller, holding a post at Leipzig in 1887.

Heinrich Zimmer (1851–1910) was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher. He studied at Tübingen, Strasbourg, and Berlin under scholars including von Roth, Goldschmidt, Weber, Scherer, and Windisch. He held posts at Berlin, Greifswald, Heidelberg, and Columbia University.

Heinrich von Stietencron (1933–2018) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Munich, SOAS London, and Heidelberg (Habilitation c. 1968–1972). He served as an assistant at Heidelberg (1965) and held a chair at Tübingen (1973–1998).

Heinz Bechert (1932–2005) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Munich, Hamburg, and Mainz, also studying under Erich Frauwallner. His main academic posts included positions at Saarland University, Mainz, and the Chair of Indology at Göttingen (1965–2000).

Heinz Mode (1913–1992) was a scholar of oriental archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Berlin and Basel under G. P. Malalasekera and Otto Fischer. He spent his career at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1948 to 1978.

Helen Baroni (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt. She took up a post at the University of Hawaiʻi around 1993.

Helen Hardacre (born 1949) specializes in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under Joseph M. Kitagawa and Jonathan Z. Smith. She held posts at Princeton (1980–1989), Griffith (1990–1992), and Harvard (from 1992).

Helen Wang (born 1965) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and sinology. She studied at SOAS University of London and became Curator of East Asian Money at the British Museum around 1993.
Helena Blankleder is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).
Helena Michie (born 1958) studied at the University of Pennsylvania (c. 1979–1984) and held a post at Rice University around 1990.

Helga Uebach (1940–2021) was a scholar in Tibetology and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Munich (c. 1961–1967) and served as an editorial consultant at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities beginning in 1964.
Hellfried Dahlmann (1905–1988) was a scholar in linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Marburg (c. 1935–1945) and the University of Cologne (c. 1951–1971).

Hellmut Wilhelm (1905–1990) was a sinologist who studied at Frankfurt, Kiel, Grenoble, and Berlin (doctorate under Otto Franke). He taught German at Peking University (c. 1933–1948) and held the chair of sinology at the University of Washington (1948–1971).

Hellmuth Hecker (1923–2017) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (PhD c. 1945–1948) and under Paul Debes (1945), later serving as a Referent at the Forschungsstelle für Völkerrecht und Ausländisches Öffentliches Recht (c. 1952–1988).

Helmer Smith (1882–1956) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Uppsala and under K. F. Johansson, R. Pischel, and K. F. Geldner. He held posts at Lund (1921) and Uppsala (1936–1947).

Helmut Eimer (1936–2023) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the universities of Hamburg, Berlin, and Bonn (Promotion c. 1968–1974) under Frank-Richard Hamm, and held a post at the University of Bonn (c. 1974–2001).

Helmut Hoffmann (1912–1992) worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Freiburg, Berlin, and Marburg, also under Lüders, Lessing, and Tucci. He held posts at the Prussian Academy, Munich (1948–1968), and Indiana University (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser (1956–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his Promotion and Habilitation at the University of Vienna, holding posts there, at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and as director of IKGA (2007–2014).

Helmut Rix (1926–2004) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg (PhD 1947–1950), and Tübingen (Habilitation c. 1955–1959). He held positions at Tübingen, Augustana-Hochschule Neuendettelsau, Regensburg, and was a professor at Freiburg (1982–1993).

Helmut Tauscher (born 1953) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner, served as a professor at the University of Vienna (attested 2010–2015), and was a Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.
